title: Rowing a Greek Warship in Battle
hook: Sitting shoulder-to-shoulder with 170 sweaty men in 100-degree heat, blind to incoming enemy rams.

scenes.text: The Athenian trireme was the deadliest warship of the ancient Mediterranean: a swift wooden missile propelled by one hundred seventy oarsmen.

scenes.text: Contrary to movie myths, Greek rowers were not enslaved convicts in chains—they were free Athenian citizens paid a full daily wage.

scenes.text: Inside the narrow wooden hull, rowers were stacked on three tiered benches, packed so closely their noses touched the back of the man ahead.

scenes.text: Heat reached over one hundred degrees, smelling of sweat and bilge water, while rowers rowed blind to flute rhythms, unable to see enemy ships.
